name: BridgeMind
tagline: An AI learning platform: courses, guided lessons and hands-on practice aimed at people trying to get productive with AI and cloud tooling.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is the boring part: a course player, a progress bar, a quiz engine, some sandbox environments. An agent can produce all of that in an afternoon and it will feel fine. What it cannot produce is the curriculum, the sequencing, the exercises that were rewritten after ten thousand people got stuck in the same place, or the credential that means anything to anyone else. A self-built version is a study harness you fill with your own material, which is a real thing to want, but it is not this product. If you are paying for structure and someone else's judgment about what to learn next, you cannot one-shot that.
coreLoopDIY: A local study app that ingests your own notes, docs and links as a curriculum, generates lessons and quizzes with an LLM, and tracks what you actually retained.
requirements: Your own source material: markdown, PDFs, links
whatYouLose: The curriculum itself, which is the entire product
Vetted exercise sets and hands-on labs that are known to work
Any credential or completion signal another human recognizes
Instructor updates when tools and models change under you
Community, cohorts and anyone to be stuck alongside
moatNotes: Education platforms live or die on content and the sense that someone competent chose the order. Neither ships in a repo.
whyPeopleStillPay: People do not buy a learning platform for the video player. They buy the decision of what to learn, in what order, with exercises that fail in instructive ways instead of confusing ones. Building your own study tool gets you a place to put material, and then you are the one who has to find and sequence the material, which is exactly the job you were trying to outsource. Add the fact that a completion badge from a known platform occasionally moves a hiring conversation and a local SQLite table does not, and the payment makes sense.
notes: The course player is a weekend; the course is not. The moat is curriculum plus the credibility that makes finishing it mean something.
prompt:
Build a local-first self-study app called "studyharness". Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle for schema and migrations, Tailwind, shadcn/ui. One repo, pnpm, runs with `pnpm dev` on port 3000. Data lives in ./data/study.db.

Core loop:
1. I drop files into ./material (markdown, txt, PDF) or paste URLs in the UI. Parse PDFs with pdf-parse, fetch URLs and strip to text with readability.
2. Chunk each source, store chunks in SQLite with source metadata.
3. "Build a track": I give a goal in plain English, the app asks an LLM to sequence the ingested material into an ordered list of lessons, each lesson pointing at specific chunks. Store the track and lesson order.
4. Lesson view: LLM writes a short explainer grounded only in the linked chunks, always shows the source chunk underneath so I can catch it lying.
5. After each lesson, generate 5 questions: 3 recall, 2 applied. Free-text answers, graded by the LLM with a short reason. Store score.
6. Spaced repetition: SM-2 lite over questions I missed. A "Due today" queue on the home page.

LLM access: one provider, OpenAI-compatible chat completions, key from OPENAI_API_KEY in .env.local. Put all calls behind lib/llm.ts with a single function so the model name is one constant. If the key is missing, the app still runs and lesson generation shows a clear disabled state.

In scope: ingest, track building, lesson view, quizzes, grading, review queue, per-track progress, export everything to JSON.

Out of scope, do not build: user auth, payments, video hosting, multi-user, certificates, mobile app, a community feed, any hosted deployment config.

Quality bar: seed with 3 sample markdown files so the loop is demoable on first run. README with setup in under 10 lines. Keep it under roughly 1500 lines of app code and prefer server actions over building an API surface I will never call.
